LESSON: NAMING SPEAKING

Grade: PP2
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.6: Naming SPEAKING

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Naming SPEAKING. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. Name objects, animals, rhymes related to colours. find in our people and colours in the •
2. Name unsafe objects in the objects in the immediate 3.

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: NAMING SPEAKING
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Naming SPEAKING helps you succeed in LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: NAMING SPEAKING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Name objects, animals, rhymes related to colours. find in our people and colours in the •

What this means
In this part you learn to Name objects, animals, rhymes related to colours. find in our people and colours in the •. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: Name objects, animals, rhymes related to colours. find in our people and colours in the •.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Naming SPEAKING”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can Name objects, animals, rhymes related to colours. find in our people and colours in the •. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Name unsafe objects in the objects in the immediate 3.

What this means
In this part you learn to Name unsafe objects in the objects in the immediate 3.. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: Name unsafe objects in the objects in the immediate 3..
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Naming SPEAKING to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can Name unsafe objects in the objects in the immediate 3.. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Naming SPEAKING is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Naming SPEAKING”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: Name objects, animals, rhymes related to colours. find in our people and colours in the •)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Naming SPEAKING to a partner. (skill: Name unsafe objects in the objects in the immediate 3.)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Naming SPEAKING to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: Name objects, animals, rhymes related to colours. find in our people and colours in the •.
3. Practise this skill: Name unsafe objects in the objects in the immediate 3..
4. Make one local Kenya example of Naming SPEAKING from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Naming SPEAKING: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP2 learner study Naming SPEAKING?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Naming SPEAKING means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: Name objects, animals, rhymes related to colours. find in our people and colours in the •.
5. Be able to: Name unsafe objects in the objects in the immediate 3..

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
